title: Continue-token path detection must key off search-specific fields, not absence of store fields
answers: Why did a client get a 400 continuing a paginated LIST after the routing gate changed mid-rollout?
How do I tell whether a ListRequest continue token came from the search path or the store/SQL scan path?
Why does tokenFromOtherListPath check SearchAfter/SearchBefore instead of Name/Namespace?
body: Symptom: a client mid-pagination on the store scan got its next page rejected (or silently restarted) once the routing gate started picking search for the same request shape. Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:tokenFromOtherListPath originally inferred a store-scan token from Name/Namespace being empty, but the SQL backend's token encodes only a row offset and has no Name either, so it was misclassified as a search token. Fix pattern: detect the search path positively (len(token.SearchAfter)>0 || len(token.SearchBefore)>0) since search always sorts by at least title_phrase and name and so always has sort values; treat everything else as a store token. Constraints: a client that started paging on the store scan must stay on the store scan for the rest of that page sequence (checked via req.NextPageToken before routing); the reverse (search token hitting a store-only build) still correctly 400s, since that only happens on rollback and the client retries fresh.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/resource continue-token handling across search and store/SQL list paths
says: Pagination breaks with 400 when routing gate switches mid-rollout
Next page fails after store gets replaced with search
Client's continue token rejected when gateway routes differently
Safely migrate pagination from one backend to another
Token becomes invalid changing pagination from store to search
search: Continue-token path detection must positively identify search tokens by presence of sort fields (len(token.SearchAfter)>0 || len(token.SearchBefore)>0), not by absence of store fields like empty Name/Namespace. Original code misclassified SQL backend tokens as search tokens because both lack Name fields; search always sorts by at least title_phrase and name, so search tokens always carry sort values. Constraint: a client mid-pagination on store scan must stay on store scan for the entire sequence (enforced via req.NextPageToken before routing); the reverse case (search token hitting store-only build) correctly 400s on rollback and client retries fresh. Applies when handling pagination tokens across search and store/SQL list code paths. Path: pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:tokenFromOtherListPath.
